votes.reasoning: AnthropicProvider.swift planLabel() (~:146-151) now only returns the memoized value, so decode never touches the Keychain on the cache-hit or stale-fallback paths. With !forceRefresh it first primes the label through readOffPool, a GCD thread (primeLabelCacheOffPoolIfNeeded, ~:155-161, called at :54). Reverted to HEAD: anthropic_cache_hit_plan_label_reads_off_pool went RED (poolReads 1). Restored, and it passes. Caveats: (a) forceRefresh + fetch failure + empty labelCache now shows a nil label in the stale fallback, where it used to read. That is acceptable, because that read would most likely have failed too. (b) On a cold start (cache miss, labelCache nil), the priming adds one extra off-pool read before the fetch reads again. That costs performance, not correctness.

planLabel() is now memo-only (AnthropicProvider.swift:148). It takes the lock, uses defer, and returns. It lost its double lock/unlock and no longer reads the Keychain from decode, so the function got shorter. The priming moved to primeLabelCacheOffPoolIfNeeded() (AnthropicProvider.swift:157), which uses readOffPool. Its `try?` is on a path that really is best-effort (only the label is lost), the doc comment says the fetch path reads again and surfaces the error, and CLAUDE.md allows `try?` for that. The extra read on a cold miss is cheap: KeychainCredentialReader.read() returns the in-memory lastKnownGood (KeychainCredentialReader.swift:56), and after a failure the security-tool fallback is in cooldown.

AnthropicProvider.swift:50-55 and :146-161 are confined to this finding. planLabel() is now memo-only, and priming moved to an async readOffPool before fetcher.run. The snapshot shape and planLabel semantics are unchanged, so the golden tests are unaffected. One cost is introduced; it is recorded in new_findings for the performance lens.
